decisions.question: Which milestone is rendered into stories in this run?
decisions.rationale: M2 (disbursement, schedule, repayment, dashboard, EOD job) depends on application/decision contracts M1 publishes; rendered in a later run.

decisions.question: How is M1 split into epics?
decisions.rationale: E1 Foundation & auth (seed users, roles, health, JSON logs, correlation ID); E2 Customer application (products, apply, documents, submit); E3 Decisioning (scoring stub, underwriting, policy violation, underwriter verify/review/override); E4 Policy admin (editor v2, admin approval, append-only). Each is a vertical slice.

decisions.question: How are the 8 NFRs (no observable criterion) handled?
decisions.rationale: Author one observable criterion per NFR and render guard/test stories in E1, attached as constraints to stories touching money, logs, routes or migrations.

decisions.question: Which dependencies are real rather than defensive?
decisions.rationale: E1 -> E2 -> E3 is real (decisioning needs submitted applications). E4 depends only on E1 and the policy file, so it can run parallel to E2/E3. Scoring stub (FR-3) is independent.
